transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

It's pretty embarrassing to admit, but I get stuck in front of the mirror or looking at photos of myself, trying to fix how I look. It’s starting to mess with my work and my runs, and my sister basically forced me to come in. I just don't know how to stop doing it.
Can you tell me more about what specifically you're trying to fix when you look at yourself, is it a particular part of your body or your overall appearance?

It’s my face—it just looks completely battered and crooked, like my nose is bent, my jaw is off, and my skin looks like old leather. I end up picking at my skin and shaving over and over, constantly worrying that I look totally lopsided to everyone else. It's incredibly frustrating and I feel so self-conscious about it.

Do you ever experience any intrusive thoughts or images that aren't related to your appearance, such as fears of harm coming to yourself or others, or repetitive thoughts that you feel compelled to act on?
No, I don't experience those kinds of thoughts or fears about harm at all. My worries and all these repetitive habits are almost entirely focused on my appearance and how bad my face looks.
Do you believe that your perceived flaws in your appearance are real, or do you have any doubts that they might be exaggerated or not noticeable to others?

They feel completely real and obvious to me, not exaggerated at all. When I look in the mirror or at photos, I clearly see that my nose is bent, my jaw is off, and my skin looks like old leather. It feels so noticeable that I constantly ask my sister and kids if I look "lopsided" because I'm terrified everyone else is seeing the same awful things I am.
Do you think that others can see these flaws in your appearance as clearly as you do, or do you believe they might be missing something that is obvious to you?

I'm convinced that everyone else sees these flaws just as clearly as I do, and that they must be judging me for how crooked and weathered my face looks. Even though my sister and kids tell me it's not that bad, I feel like they're just trying to be nice to spare my feelings. To me, there is no way people can look at me and not notice how lopsided I am.

Do you ever have moments where you can step back and think that maybe your concerns about your appearance are not entirely based in reality, or do you always believe your perceptions of your flaws are accurate?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about whether my mind is playing tricks on me or if it's unrealistic. All I know is that when I'm looking in the mirror, those flaws feel completely real and it's just incredibly distressing to me. In those moments, I really can't see it any other way.

Have you ever considered seeking a plastic surgeon's opinion or a dermatologist's evaluation to assess the actual physical appearance of your face, or do you believe that even a professional's assessment would not change your perception of your flaws?
I haven't really thought about seeing a plastic surgeon or a dermatologist. Honestly, I'd feel way too embarrassed and self-conscious to even have a professional look at me that closely.

Have you ever had any experiences or instances where you were convinced of something being true about your appearance, but later found out or were shown that it wasn't as you thought, or has your belief in your perceived flaws always remained consistent?

I'm not really sure, but my belief in these flaws has always been completely consistent. I've never had a moment where I realized I was wrong or that it wasn't as bad as I thought. To me, it has always just looked crooked and wrong every single time I look in the mirror.

Have you ever experienced a time when you were completely alone and not thinking about your appearance, and then something triggered you to start focusing on your flaws again, or is it something that's always on your mind?

While the worry is always lurking in the background, there are definitely specific triggers that set off the really intense episodes. Seeing close-up photos of myself from work or the running club on social media, or just catching my reflection in a mirror, immediately starts it. Once that happens, I'll get stuck for hours zooming in on my face and trying to "fix" how I look.

Do you think it's possible that your concerns about your appearance might be exaggerated or not based in reality, or do you firmly believe that your perceptions of your flaws are accurate and would be confirmed by others?

I firmly believe these flaws are completely real and obvious. Even though my sister and kids try to reassure me when I ask them, I can't help but see my crooked nose, off-center jaw, and weathered skin as completely undeniable whenever I look in the mirror or zoom in on photos. To me, it just feels like a physical reality that anyone looking closely would immediately notice.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms and behaviors are consistent with Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD), characterized by a preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance, which are not observable or appear slight to others. The patient's repetitive behaviors, such as excessive checking and attempting to fix their appearance, and their distress and impairment in social and occupational functioning, support this diagnosis.
